h1:
Mookata & Thai BBQ
in Tak and Mae Sot
intro: In Tak and Mae Sot, the dinner locals get together for most often is mookata — Thai BBQ hot pot. One pan feeds the whole table, and you start at under 200 THB a head. Plenty of spots are all-you-can-eat with grilled seafood thrown in at a single price. We've picked the best on both the Tak city side and the Mae Sot side, sticking to places that are actually open and where locals eat regularly.

blocks.html: Mookata suits Tak and Mae Sot well. These are small towns, the evening air turns pleasant, and a big group can happily gather around the pan. Most spots are all-you-can-eat at a single price — pork, beef, chicken, grilled seafood, vegetables, fried bits, all the way down to shaved ice for dessert. We've ordered these by ones that are easy to find and that locals genuinely go to. Prices are rough ranges and shift with daily promos and ingredients, so check the restaurant's page before you go to be sure.

blocks.text: Our picks, ordered by how often locals go

items.name: Mookata Khon Kep Fuen (Mae Sot)
items.blurb: One of the top names Mae Sot locals point you to, and very easy to find since it sits on the Asia Highway next to Lotus's Extra Mae Sot. It's airy with lots of tables, has parking, and the buffet includes drinking water. Great for big groups or families. It packs out on weekend evenings, so come a bit early to grab a good table.
items.meta: Mae Sot · Asia Highway, next to Lotus's Extra

items.name: Seafood Buffet — Grilled Seafood & Mookata (Tak city)
items.blurb: On the Tak city side, this one stands out for grilled seafood — squid, prawns, and shellfish all rolled into a single-price buffet. Pair it with a rich-broth mookata and finish on shaved ice and old-style ice cream. It's by the foot of Kittikhajorn Bridge at the mouth of Soi Chiang Thong, so it's easy to get in and out. Good for seafood lovers who want it unlimited.
items.meta: Tak city · foot of Kittikhajorn Bridge, mouth of Soi Chiang Thong

items.name: MAPPA Shabu — BBQ & Shabu (Tak city)
items.blurb: If you want something a bit more modern, this place charges one NET price with no add-ons, and does both grill and shabu under one roof. Premium items like salmon, sliced beef, and the house shrimp dumplings round it out. The room is comfortable to sit in, good for a group of friends or a couple who want something warm on a cool evening.

items.name: Jay Ah Mookata Buffet (Mae Sot)
items.blurb: Another grilled-seafood buffet on the Mae Sot side that locals bring up often. The spread is varied — pork, chicken, and seafood at one price — and it's an easy, budget-friendly dinner for a big group. Check the restaurant's page for opening hours and current promos before you head over.
items.meta: Mae Sot · within Mae Sot municipality

items.name: Biu Biu Seafood Shabu & Mookata Buffet (Mae Sot)
items.blurb: This one combines seafood shabu and mookata together — boil it or grill it, you can do both at the same table. Perfect for a group where some prefer simmering and others prefer grilling, so nobody has to argue over which place to go.

items.name: Mookata 2in1 (in both Tak and Mae Sot)
items.blurb: A mookata-and-shabu-in-one-pan style spot, with branches on both the Tak city side and the Mae Sot side, so it's handy wherever you are. An easy, good-value dinner option for anyone who wants both the broth and the grill at once.

items.name: New BBQ-Shabu spot in Mae Sot (salmon & grilled river prawns)
items.blurb: A newer Mae Sot opening that leans on unlimited salmon and grilled river prawns. NET price with water included, no add-ons. Open daily from late morning through late evening, good for anyone after premium picks who wants to eat a lot of grilled prawns on a buffet budget.

items.name: Mookata 5 Or (Mae Sot)
items.blurb: A regular mookata grill spot in Mae Sot that makes for a no-fuss dinner choice. Easy to eat, easy on the wallet — good for a night when you want a hot mookata near your hotel without driving far.

blocks.title: How to pick a spot
blocks.html: Most grilled-seafood buffets in Tak and Mae Sot are a single all-you-can-eat price, but that price moves with ingredients and the promo of the moment. Before you go, message the restaurant's page to ask the day's price and whether water is included, so the bill doesn't surprise you. Friday and Saturday evenings get busy — if you're in a big group, call to book a table first to be safe.

Overall, mookata and BBQ around here are good value, since these are provincial towns. Per-person prices start in the low hundreds for a standard mookata buffet. If you want grilled seafood or premium items like salmon and sliced beef, it climbs into the high 200s to low 300s — still easy on the wallet compared with the big cities.

items: Standard mookata buffet — around ฿150–200 a head, unlimited, good for a budget night out with friends
Grilled-seafood buffet — around ฿230–260 a head, with unlimited prawns, shellfish, and squid
Premium BBQ-shabu — around ฿280–300 NET, with salmon and sliced beef, one all-in price
Drinks — many spots include water in the price, so check before you order more

blocks.text: Tak city vs. Mae Sot — what's the difference?

items.name: Tak city side
items.blurb: Spots cluster around the town center, near Kittikhajorn Bridge and along the Ping River. Strong on grilled seafood and more modern BBQ. Good if you're staying in central Tak.

items.name: Mae Sot side
items.blurb: More spots and more variety, since Mae Sot is a lively border town. Easy to find along the Asia Highway and within the municipality. Good if you're visiting Mae Sot and the Moei River.

faq.q: Which mookata is good in Mae Sot?
faq.a: The one Mae Sot locals recommend most often is Mookata Khon Kep Fuen, on the Asia Highway next to Lotus's Extra — easy to find, airy, with parking, and a buffet from about 189 THB a head. Jay Ah Mookata Buffet and Biu Biu Seafood Shabu are also regular go-tos for people around here.

faq.q: Is there mookata or BBQ in Tak city itself?
faq.a: Yes. The standout in Tak city is the Grilled Seafood & Mookata buffet near the foot of Kittikhajorn Bridge at the mouth of Soi Chiang Thong — a buffet around 239 THB with unlimited grilled seafood — and MAPPA Shabu, a single-price NET BBQ-shabu around 299 THB with salmon and sliced beef.

faq.q: How much is mookata in Tak and Mae Sot per person?
faq.a: A standard mookata buffet starts around 150–200 THB a head. A grilled-seafood buffet runs around 230–260 THB, and premium BBQ-shabu with items like salmon sits around 280–300 THB NET — good value compared with the big cities.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table ahead?
faq.a: On weekdays you can mostly just walk in, but Friday and Saturday evenings and long weekends get fairly packed. If you're going in a big group, call to book or message the restaurant's page first, and arrive early in the evening for a better table.

faq.q: How reliable are the prices listed here?
faq.a: The prices given are rough ranges based on the latest restaurant info and reviews, but buffets often adjust with ingredients and current promos. Before you go, check the restaurant's page or call to confirm the day's price to be sure.
